request_payload.title: Clinical variability of neurofibromatosis 1: A modifying role of cooccurring PTPN11 variants and atypical brain MRI findings.

mentions.sentence: Neurofibromatosis 1 (NF1) is a disorder characterized by variable expressivity caused by loss-of-function variants in NF1, encoding neurofibromin, a protein negatively controlling RAS signaling.

mentions.sentence: Three subjects were heterozygous for a gain-of-function variant and showed a severe expression of NF1 (developmental delay, multiple cerebral neoplasms and peculiar cortical MRI findings), and features resembling Noonan syndrome (a RASopathy caused by activating variants in PTPN11).

Three subjects were heterozygous for a gain-of-function variant and showed a severe expression of NF1 (developmental delay, multiple cerebral neoplasms and peculiar cortical MRI findings), and features resembling Noonan syndrome (a RASopathy caused by activating variants in PTPN11).
Conversely, the fourth subject, who showed an attenuated presentation, carried a previously unreported PTPN11 variant that had a hypomorphic behavior in vitro.
